A_target.statement:
Let $f$ be a [[Definition:Continuous Real Function|continuous]] $2 \pi$-[[Definition:Periodic Real Function|periodic]] function.
Let $\displaystyle \sigma_N f = \frac 1 N \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^{N - 1} S_n f$ be the [[Definition:Cesàro Summation|Cesàro means]] of its [[Definition:Fourier Series|Fourier series]].
Then $\sigma_N f \to f$ [[Definition:Uniform Convergence|uniformly]].

B_source.statement:
The [[Definition:Fejér Kernel|Fejér kernel]] $\displaystyle F_N = \frac 1 N \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^{N - 1} D_n$ satisfies:
:$\map {F_N} x = \dfrac 1 N \paren {\dfrac {\map \sin {N x / 2} } {\map \sin {x / 2} } }^2 \ge 0, \quad \dfrac 1 {2 \pi} \displaystyle \int_{-\pi}^\pi F_N = 1$

derived.an approximate identity: uniform convergence by splitting near and far from 0

object_map.reformulation: Average the partial sums so that the kernel becomes non-negative and concentrates at 0.

validity_conditions: Positivity of the kernel is essential; the Dirichlet kernel has unbounded L1 norm and partial sums can diverge.
Uniform continuity of f on a period controls the contribution near 0.
proof_plan: By linearity, $\sigma_N f = f * F_N$, where convolution is normalized by $\dfrac 1 {2 \pi}$.

By the source result, $F_N \ge 0$ with mean $1$.
For $\delta \le \size x \le \pi$:
:$\map {F_N} x \le \dfrac 1 {N \map {\sin^2} {\delta / 2} } \to 0$

Hence:
:$\displaystyle \size {\map {\sigma_N f} x - \map f x} \le \frac 1 {2 \pi} \int_{-\pi}^\pi \map {F_N} t \size {\map f {x - t} - \map f x} \rd t$
Split the integral into $\size t < \delta$ and $\size t \ge \delta$.

By [[Heine-Cantor Theorem|uniform continuity]], the first part is less than $\epsilon$ for suitable $\delta$.
The second is at most $2 \norm f_\infty \sup_{\size t \ge \delta} \map {F_N} t \to 0$, uniformly in $x$.
This is [[Fejér's Theorem]].
{{qed}}
